title.title: Positive scalar curvature forces rational inessentiality
title.subtitle: Claim: no closed aspherical manifold of any dimension carries positive scalar curvature, spin or not

plain: Big, endlessly unrolling shapes like a torus can never curve like a ball everywhere, in any dimension

beats.text: Schematically: positive scalar curvature makes small balls a little smaller
Minimal surfaces and $\mu$-bubbles reached dimension 5; Dirac operators need spin
The claim reshapes the metric one warped circle at a time, at a logarithmic cost

steps: Suppose such a space had positive curvature; get a map to a sphere
Add warped circles one at a time, shrinking the map at a small cost
Eventually a known obstruction is broken: impossible

voice.text: Positive scalar curvature makes small balls smaller. Aspherical spaces should never allow it.

Claimed: true in every dimension, spin or not.
